    `foreign import javascript`. Do NOT touch site/cabal.project.

    the whole codebase, reachable only from an explicit learner click. Never at
    boot, never from feature detection. Never with sysex.

    nothing added to ProgressEvent or the M3 progress sink.

    scripts/check-site.sh. NO M4 TASK MAY EDIT WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES. The
    task-local budget is in briefs/M4-budget.json, written by wave 0.

    browser without Web MIDI the app must look and behave exactly as M3 did --
    the only permitted DOM difference is the always-hidden #sxc1-device-state node.

    check and it passed" is not evidence; "I broke the thing it checks, watched it
    fail with the right message, and put it back" is.

  * any file under content/ (no content edits, no new exercises, no verify: edits)

    content format, the validator and their issue codes are frozen

  * WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES

    asyncCallback1), enumerate MIDIInputMap via Array.from(inputs.values()),
    install onmidimessage via setProp, read MIDIMessageEvent.data bytes via
    (! "length") and (!! k), unsubscribe with jsNull + freeFunction, and dispatch a
    Miso action from inside a JS callback.

    must write `import Prelude hiding ((!!))` together with `import Miso.DSL ((!!))`.

    promise. The denied path is therefore exercised for free, and a target with no
    injected fake is a valid negative control.

    1,000,000-byte ceiling.

  content/exercises/10-pad-play-banks.ex.md       d-2-01 step 1  verify: cc 80 127
  content/exercises/20-pad-play-sounds.ex.md      d-2-02 step 1  verify: pad 1 bank A
  content/exercises/20-pad-play-sounds.ex.md      d-2-02 step 2  verify: pad 13 bank A

  content/exercises/30-pad-play-performance.ex.md d-2-09 step 2  verify: cc 108 127
  content/exercises/30-pad-play-performance.ex.md d-2-09 step 3  verify: cc 109 127
Routes: #/x/pad-play-banks/d-2-01 , #/x/pad-play-sounds/d-2-02 ,
        #/x/pad-play-performance/d-2-09

unreachable in practice -- CC 16 is a continuous dial, not a 0/127 button. That is
a known content defect deferred to M5. Do not "fix" it and do not write a test
that depends on it firing.

  . "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"
  cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site && wasm32-wasi-cabal build -j2 exe:app
  cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1 && ./scripts/build-site.sh
  cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1 && ./scripts/check-site.sh
  "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/wasm-run/bin/wasm-run.mjs" "$(wasm32-wasi-cabal list-bin exe:exercise-check | tail -1)" --self-test

  node scripts/browser-check.mjs --self-test-negative

YOU ARE WAVE 3, running in parallel with device-protocol. You wire M4's browser
work into the repository's single acceptance gate.

You own exactly these paths:
    scripts/check-site.sh
    scripts/build-site.sh
Do not edit scripts/browser-check.mjs or scripts/fake-midi.js (wave 2 owns them),
site/** or content/**.

Read scripts/check-site.sh's leading comment block first. It documents the
result=complete / result=structural-only discipline, the two skip axes
(--skip-browser and --skip-content), the ok()/fail()/skip()/info() counters, and
M0's finding n2 that invariant greps must be anchored to non-comment lines.

ABSOLUTE RULES

 1. ADD NO NEW SKIP AXIS. M4's checks live on the EXISTING BROWSER AXIS: they are
    skipped by --skip-browser / SXC1_SKIP_BROWSER=1 through skip(), never by a new
    switch. M2 made the same ruling for the content axis, for the same reason --
    one fewer switch is one fewer route to result=complete without having checked.
 2. Every skipped check must still increment TOTAL through skip(), so the TOTAL is
    identical between a full run and a skipped run. M2's L2 fix exists because that
    invariant was once broken; do not break it again.
 3. NEVER edit WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES. It stays 1000000.

ADD THESE CHECKS (each with the same message style as its neighbours):

  V1  WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES is literally 1000000 and app.wasm gzip is under it.
      (The existing size tripwire covers the second half; make the CONSTANT itself
      an explicit assertion so a silent raise is caught even if the artefact fits.)
  V2  app.wasm gzip is under briefs/M4-budget.json's task_local_ceiling_bytes, and
      the check prints the observed value and the delta from m3_final_gzip_bytes.
  V3  scripts/fake-midi.js exists, parses under `node --check`, and exposes every
      driver member (calls, setOutcome, addPort, removePort, emit, subscribedCount,
      ports).
  V4  NEITHER site/public NOR site/static contains fake-midi.js -- the harness fake
      is never shipped.
  V5  The M4 structural invariants, all anchored to non-comment lines
      (briefs/M4-plan.md section 5): exactly one requestMIDIAccess in site/app and
      it is in the device bridge; sysex only as False; no localStorage /
      sessionStorage / Miso.Storage under site/app/Device/ (CASE-INSENSITIVE --
      Miso's API is setLocalStorage, so a case-sensitive grep would miss it, exactly
      as M2 recorded); no fetch/getJSON/postJSON/sendBeacon/WebSocket in site/app;
      noDeviceVerifier is gone; dvWatch has a call site outside its definition;
      SXC1.Midi.Table is not reachable from exe:app.
  V6  The browser check passes with the device assertions included, on the browser
      axis, via skip() when skipped.
  V7  docs/M4-device-test-protocol.md exists, and every route id and DOM id it
      names actually exists (grep the ids out of the doc and confirm each appears
      in site/app or content/exercises). A protocol that names a control the app
      does not have is worse than no protocol.
  V8  briefs/M4-budget.json exists, is authorised, and its m3_final_gzip_bytes is
      within 3000 bytes of a freshly measured build -- so a stale budget cannot
      silently license an over-budget artefact.

build-site.sh: change it only if M4 genuinely requires it. It currently builds
exe:app exe:content-check exe:exercise-check; M4 adds no executable, so the
expected diff is EMPTY. If you find yourself editing it, say why in your report.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (mandatory, each demonstrated and reverted):
  * Raise WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES to 2000000 in a scratch copy -> V1 fails.
  * Point V2 at a task_local_ceiling_bytes of 1 -> V2 fails with the byte overage.
  * Copy scripts/fake-midi.js into site/public -> V4 fails.
  * Add a second requestMIDIAccess call in a scratch copy of site/app -> V5 fails.
  * Add a `verify: cc` id to the protocol doc that does not exist -> V7 fails.
  * Run with SXC1_SKIP_BROWSER=1 -> the run reports result=structural-only, the
    device checks are SKIPPED (not silently absent), and TOTAL is UNCHANGED from
    the full run. Paste both TOTALs side by side.
  * Confirm no new skip flag exists: `grep -c 'skip-' scripts/check-site.sh` and
    the usage() text must still describe exactly two axes.

FINAL REPORT: the check count before and after, both TOTALs from the skip
comparison, all seven negative-control outputs, and confirmation that
result=complete with zero skipped checks on a full run.

YOU ARE WAVE 3, running in parallel with verification. You write the one piece of
M4 evidence nobody else can produce: the checklist the owner follows with their
physical Casio SXC-1. Their pass/fail report is part of the M4 gate.

You own exactly this path:
    docs/                    (new directory; create docs/M4-device-test-protocol.md)
Do not edit anything else. README.md belongs to wave 4.

AUDIENCE. The owner. They own the hardware and read English; they do not read
Haskell and should not have to open a terminal. Every instruction is something
they can do with the device in one hand and a browser in the other. No jargon
without a gloss. No step whose success criterion is vague.

ACCURACY IS THE WHOLE POINT. Before you write a single instruction, BUILD AND RUN
the app and walk the protocol yourself against scripts/fake-midi.js, exactly as
wave 2's browser-check does. Every route, every button label, every id and every
sentence you quote must be the one the app actually renders. Wave 3's check V7
greps the ids out of your document and fails if any of them does not exist.
A protocol that names a control the app does not have is worse than none.

 1. Prerequisites.

      headless/automation browser -- measured 2026-08-07, headless Chrome exposes
      the API but always denies the permission.
    * SXC-1 firmware: translations/midi.md says MIDI IN/OUT and Control Change
      arrived in Ver. 1.1.1, and the document itself describes Ver. 1.3.0. Tell
      them how to check, and cite the manual page.
    * A USB cable that carries data.
    * How to see and set MIDI OUT Ch. on the unit: long-press EDIT to enter system
      settings, scroll to "MIDI OUT Ch.", left/right to change, EDIT to exit.
      Cite translations/midi.md section 1.1 and its page.

    nobody in this project has: it decides whether the port matcher can be
    tightened later. Say so, so they understand why it matters.

    currently accepts a pad press whatever the velocity is; their number confirms
    whether that was necessary.

    a few clicks never produces either. This is recorded as finding M4-F1 and is

    bug -- reporting it as WORKING would be the surprise.

    A on the drill's step 1, and confirm the page says it received MIDI on channel
    3 while listening on channel 1; click the offered switch; press A again; it
    should confirm. Then set the unit back to 1.

    port listed; permission denied or never asked; the page confirms the wrong
    step; nothing happens at all. End every row with the reassurance that the
    manual Confirm button always works and no drill can be blocked by MIDI.

    version, the exact port name, the captured lastMessage bytes, one line per
    numbered step above with PASS/FAIL/NA, and free-text notes.

line. No screenshots (they would go stale). Every claim about the device cites
translations/midi.md with a section and page. Keep it to something a person can
work through in about fifteen minutes.

route id and DOM id the document names together with where each one exists in the
